items.title: Top 5 Longest Years in the Solar System (#1 Lasts 11,400 Years) #shorts
items.description:
One year = one trip around the Sun. Five far worlds, their orbits drawn to scale.
Full video: How Long to Reach Every Planet? By Car, Neptune Takes 4,912 Years

Sources
• NASA Science (Pluto): one orbit takes 248 Earth years; Pluto was discovered in 1930
• NASA Science (Haumea): one orbit takes about 285 Earth years; its fast spin stretches it into an elongated shape
• JPL Small-Body Database: Makemake orbital period about 309 years; Eris about 557 years; Sedna about 11,400 years (semi-major axis about 506 AU, eccentricity about 0.85)
• Farming began roughly 12,000 to 11,000 years ago (Neolithic Revolution, Encyclopaedia Britannica)
• Own calculations: Kepler's third law P = a^1.5 (years, AU) as a check; 1930 + 248 = 2178; 2026 - 309 = 1717; 557 / 250 (USA since 1776) ≈ 2.2; 11,400 / 248 ≈ 46

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.title: The Moon's Entire Orbit Fits Inside the Sun #shorts
items.description:
Put Earth at the centre of the Sun: the Moon's whole orbit fits inside, with 311,600 km to spare. Drawn to scale.
Full video: What If the Moon Crashed Into Earth? You'd Have 4 Days

Sources
• NASA Science, Sun facts: the Sun is about 1,392,000 km (865,000 miles) wide, so its radius is about 696,000 km
• NASA Science, Moon facts: average distance from Earth 384,400 km (about 405,500 km at its farthest)
• NASA, Apollo 11 mission timeline: launch 16 July 1969, entered lunar orbit 19 July 1969 (about 76 hours)
• Own calculations: 696,000 - 384,400 = 311,600 km to spare (290,500 km with the Moon at its farthest); 1,392,000 / 768,800 ≈ 1.8; Apollo 11 average pace 384,400 km / 76 h ≈ 5,060 km/h, so 1,392,000 km takes about 275 h ≈ 11.5 days

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
